info.name: user-template API
info.description:
Every endpoint of the API, in the same structure as the routes.

**Setup** (see postman/README.md in the repo):
1. Postman Vault > settings: enable **support in Postman scripts**, and allow this collection.
2. Add vault secrets `loginEmail` (your email, also used to register), `loginPassword` (also the password you register with) and `newPassword` (used by Change password and Reset password), and set the `registerUsername` collection variable.
3. Run **Auth > Login**. The session token is stored in the vault as `authToken`.

Authed requests inherit the collection's Bearer auth (`{{vault:authToken}}`). Public ones are set to No Auth. The token is refreshed automatically when it's past half its life, so it only needs a new login after 2 hours idle.

Requests that come from an email link use the `linkToken` variable: paste the last part of the link into it.

exec: // Keeps the stored session alive: once the token is past half its life it's swapped for a fresh one.
// Refreshing keeps the original login time, so it doesn't count as a fresh login.
console.warn("The session has expired: run Auth > Login again");
.catch(() => console.warn("Can't read the vault: enable vault support in scripts"));

item.name: Two-factor
item.description: Authenticator app codes. Setup answers the secret (add it to an app by hand, or turn `otpauthUrl` into a QR code), and Enable turns 2FA on with a code from the app. From then on Login answers a challenge, and Verify trades it plus a code for the session. Put the current code (or a backup code) in `twoFactorCode`.

Uses the `twoFactorToken` Login left. Stores the session token in the vault.

item.name: OAuth
item.description: Sign in with Google (Apple works the same way, with `apple` in the path and no PKCE). Run **Authorization URL**, open the `url` it answers in a browser and sign in. Google then sends you to `FRONTEND_URL/auth/oauth/google/callback?code=...`. Without a frontend that page won't load, so copy the `code` from the address bar into `oauthCode` right away (it expires within minutes) and run **Login**. The provider has to be configured in the .env.

request.description: The configured providers, and whether each one uses PKCE.
Generates the state, nonce and PKCE values, and answers the Google sign-in URL to open.

exec: // What a frontend does before each sign-in: a fresh state and nonce, and a PKCE verifier
